Class.summary: Controller responsible for managing support tickets. Provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and assigning tickets. Uses role-based logic to isolate data appropriately (Admin, SupportAgent, Customer).

Constructor.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
Constructor.param: The MediatR mediator instance for dispatching queries and commands.
The service used to obtain the current authenticated user's ID and role.

GetTickets.summary: Retrieves a paginated list of support tickets with optional filtering and sorting.
GetTickets.remarks: Results are scoped automatically based on the authenticated user's role: Admin: Sees all tickets across the system. SupportAgent: Sees only tickets assigned to them. Customer: Sees only tickets that they created.
GetTickets.param: Pagination, filtering (Status, Priority, Search), and sorting parameters.
GetTickets.returns: A paginated response containing ticket summary DTOs and pagination metadata.
GetTickets.response: Returns the paginated list of tickets matching the query filters.
If query parameters (such as page or pageSize) are out of valid range.
If the user is not authenticated.

GetTicketById.summary: Retrieves a specific support ticket by its unique identifier.
GetTicketById.remarks: Access is restricted based on ownership and role: Admin: Can access any ticket. SupportAgent: Can only access tickets assigned to them. Customer: Can only access tickets they submitted. If the ticket is not found or the caller lacks permission, a 404 Not Found response is returned for IDOR protection.
GetTicketById.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
GetTicketById.returns: The detailed ticket information including customer and assigned agent display names.
GetTicketById.response: If the user is not authenticated.
If the ticket does not exist or the user is not authorized to view it.

CreateTicket.remarks: Only users with the Customer role can create tickets. An activity record with type Created is automatically recorded.
CreateTicket.param: The ticket details including title, description, and requested priority.
CreateTicket.returns: The newly created ticket response DTO.
CreateTicket.response: If the request fails validation (e.g. missing title, description).
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller does not have the Customer role.

UpdateTicket.summary: Updates the core details (Title, Description) of an existing ticket.
UpdateTicket.remarks: Only users with the Admin role are authorized to perform this update.
UpdateTicket.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
UpdateTicket.response: The ticket details were successfully updated.
If the update request is invalid.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller is not an administrator.
If the ticket does not exist.

UpdateTicketStatus.summary: Updates the status of a ticket according to business role rules.
UpdateTicketStatus.remarks: Role-based transition permissions: Admin: Can set any valid status. SupportAgent: Can resolve assigned tickets. Customer: Can close or reopen their own tickets. Enforces state transitions: Open tickets must be InProgress before resolving; Closed tickets can only be reopened.
UpdateTicketStatus.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
UpdateTicketStatus.response: The status was updated and an activity log entry was created.
If the transition is forbidden by role or state machine rules.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the ticket does not exist or user is unauthorized.

UpdateTicketPriority.summary: Updates the priority level of a ticket.
UpdateTicketPriority.remarks: Only users with the Admin role can change ticket priority.
UpdateTicketPriority.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
The new priority (Low, Medium, High, Critical).
UpdateTicketPriority.response: If the priority value is invalid.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller is not an administrator.
If the ticket does not exist.

AssignAgent.summary: Assigns or reassigns a Support Agent to a ticket.
AssignAgent.remarks: Only users with the Admin role can assign agents. Tickets that are already closed cannot be assigned to an agent.
AssignAgent.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
The ID of the Support Agent.
AssignAgent.response: The agent was assigned successfully and an activity audit entry was recorded.
If the ticket is closed or the user is invalid.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller is not an administrator.
If the ticket does not exist.
